newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rubber prices fall, buying modest - traders.
newsitem.headline: Thai rubber prices fall, buying modest - traders.

text.p: Thai rubber prices continued to fall this week in line with a regional market trend as activity in the market was limited, trade sources said on Wednesday.

There was market talk that the Thai government would soon send a team to Japan to boost sales of rubber to that country after the government said it planned to push China to buy 400,000 tonnes of rubber from Thailand this year.

"The market is still hanging over from the unwinding of US rubber stocks. The lower Tokyo prices also weighed the market down," said one Bangkok-based trader. "There was modest buying in the market. China bought some."
But the government which tried to shore up domestic prices by buying up to 26,400 tonnes since March 5, had not entered the market this week, trade sources said.

The Thai benchmark RSS3 rubber for May delivery slid further to 118.00-119.00 US cents a kg FOB Bangkok compared with 121.00-122.00 cents on Friday. Concentrated latex was indicated at around 90 cents.
